What We Do

Full-Service Thoracic Surgery Revenue Cycle Management

Thoracic surgery billing requires precise VATS vs. open procedure code selection, lung resection extent coding, chest wall and mediastinal procedure billing, and global period compliance. PMEX reviews every operative report before coding and manages the full claim lifecycle.

VATS Procedure Coding

Video-assisted thoracoscopic CPT codes selected from the operative report approach and procedure.

Lung Resection Billing

Wedge, segmental, lobectomy, and pneumonectomy coded by extent from the operative report.

Chest Tube Management

Mediastinoscopy Billing

Mediastinoscopy and mediastinal biopsy codes billed per the documented procedure extent.

Robotic-Assisted Coding

Global Period Compliance

90-day global periods tracked per procedure per surgeon, with post-op visits managed correctly.

Sound Familiar?

Common Thoracic Surgery Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

VATS procedure billed at open thoracotomy rate when a minimally invasive approach was used.

PMEX reads the operative report to confirm surgical approach and codes VATS vs. open per the documented technique.

Lung resection extent under-coded: lobectomy billed as wedge resection.

PMEX verifies resection extent from the operative report and codes the correct procedure level per the documented anatomy.

Post-op E/M billed during the 90-day global period without modifier 24.

PMEX tracks global period end dates per procedure and routes post-op visits to the correct billing path.

Robotic-assisted thoracic procedure submitted without the robotic add-on code.

PMEX applies the robotic surgery add-on (S2900) alongside the primary thoracic CPT code when robotic technique is documented.

Chest tube insertion denied because imaging guidance add-on not included on the claim.

PMEX bills 75989 or 76942 alongside chest tube insertion codes when imaging guidance is documented in the procedure note.

Prior authorization not confirmed before complex thoracic surgery is scheduled.

PMEX obtains surgical prior authorization with clinical documentation before the OR date is placed on the schedule.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Thoracic Surgery Billing

Thoracic surgery practices lose 14 to 24 percent of revenue to VATS miscoding, resection level errors, and global period violations.

PATTERN 01

VATS Procedure Billed as Open Thoracotomy

VATS lobectomy performed (32663). Billing team submits open lobectomy (32480). Codes have different relative value units and are distinct procedures. On payer audit, the operative report documents VATS approach. Recoupment risk created and compliance exposure established.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the operative report for the surgical approach before selecting any thoracic CPT code. VATS codes and open codes are distinct and are not interchangeable. The approach is confirmed before every submission.

PATTERN 02

Lung Resection Under-Coded

Right lower lobe lobectomy performed (32663 VATS or 32480 open). Billing team submits wedge resection code (32669 VATS or 32500 open). Lobectomy reimbursement: $1,850. Wedge: $680. $1,170 per case under-coded from one resection level error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX verifies the extent of lung resection from the operative report: wedge, segmentectomy, lobectomy, or pneumonectomy, and applies the CPT code that corresponds to the documented resection extent.

PATTERN 03

Post-Op Visit Denied During Global Period

Patient presents 4 weeks after lobectomy for routine follow-up. Standard E/M (99213) submitted. Payer denies as included in the 90-day surgical global fee. Modifier 24 was not applied, and the documented reason was not a new unrelated condition.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks the 90-day global period end date for every major thoracic procedure and confirms that post-op visit billing includes modifier 24 (new unrelated condition) or modifier 79 (unrelated procedure) with supporting documentation before submission.

Questions

Thoracic Surgery Billing Questions Answered

VATS and open procedures have separate CPT codes. The approach is determined from the operative report. We read the report before selecting any thoracic procedure code and do not apply VATS codes to open procedures or vice versa.

Wedge resection, segmentectomy, lobectomy, bilobectomy, and pneumonectomy each have separate CPT codes. We verify the extent of resection from the operative report and code the documented anatomy.

Major thoracic procedures have a 90-day global period during which routine pre-op and post-op care is included in the surgical fee. We track global period end dates and route post-op visits to the correct billing path.

Yes. Robotic-assisted thoracic procedures are billed with the primary thoracic CPT code alongside the robotic add-on code when robotic technique is documented in the operative report.

Yes. We manage surgical prior authorization with clinical documentation before the OR date is confirmed for all elective thoracic procedures.
